question.worked_solution:
Taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{7}^{x+1} & >{5}^{x-1} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({7}^{x+1}) & >\operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{x-1}) \\ (x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡7 & >(x-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡7+\operatorname{ln}⁡7 & >x\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡7-x\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & >-\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡7 \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡7-\operatorname{ln}⁡5) & >-\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡7 \\ x & >-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5+\operatorname{ln}⁡7}{\operatorname{ln}⁡7-\operatorname{ln}⁡5} \\ x & >\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5+\operatorname{ln}⁡7}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡7}\end{aligned}
$$
